meta.title: 裸辞还是骑驴找马？别轻易辞职找工作
meta.title_en: Quit First or Job-Hunt First? Don't Resign Blindly

scenes.context: 讲者描述职场人的裸辞纠结：工作到忍耐极限、没时间求职，又担心裸辞没有安全感。
sentences: 现在这工作已经到了自己忍耐的极限，必须要离职。
This job has hit the limit of what I can stand—I have to leave.
忍耐的极限：the limit of what I can stand
日常工作非常忙，没有纯粹的时间去改简历求职。
Work is so busy that there's no real time to polish my resume or job-hunt.
改简历求职：polish a resume and job-hunt
担心裸辞之后找不到理想工作，缺乏保障没有安全感。
I worry that after quitting I won't find a good job, with no safety net.
缺乏保障：no safety net
paraphrase: 裸辞冲动 = 用安全感换时间
Quitting blindly trades away your safety net for time.
纠结 → 需要算清利弊
The dilemma needs a clear pros-and-cons calculation.
scenes.speak: This job has hit the limit of what I can stand—I have to leave. Work is so busy that there's no real time to polish my resume or job-hunt. I worry that after quitting I won't find a good job, with no safety net.

scenes.title_en: The Advantage of Hunting While Employed
scenes.context: 讲者说明在职求职底气足、谈薪筹码强，不建议轻易裸辞。
sentences: 在职情况下去找工作，本身底气就足一些。
Job-hunting while still employed gives you more leverage.
底气足：more leverage
公司如果对你非常认可，会开出更优厚的条件。
If the company really wants you, it will offer better terms to win you over.
更优厚的条件：better terms
整体谈薪难度会降低很多。
That makes salary negotiation a lot easier overall.
谈薪难度：salary negotiation
paraphrase: Being employed is your bargaining chip.
公司抢你 → 条件更好
When companies compete for you, the offers get better.
scenes.speak: Job-hunting while still employed gives you more leverage. If the company really wants you, it will offer better terms to win you over. That makes salary negotiation a lot easier overall.

scenes.context: 讲者给出忙碌的解法与放手一搏的例外条件。
sentences: 工作再忙，也要把事情理个轻重缓急、有所取舍。
No matter how busy, prioritize your tasks and make trade-offs.
轻重缓急：prioritize
可以把面试约在非工作时间，比如晚上或者周末。
Schedule interviews outside work hours, like evenings or weekends.
非工作时间：outside work hours
如果工作已严重影响求职进度，可以放手一搏。
If the job is seriously hurting your job search, it's okay to go all in.
放手一搏：go all in
paraphrase: 用取舍 → 平衡求职与工作
Prioritize and make trade-offs to balance work and job-hunting.
例外才放手 → 先看影响
Only go all in when the job truly blocks your search.
scenes.speak: No matter how busy, prioritize your tasks and make trade-offs. Schedule interviews outside work hours, like evenings or weekends. If the job is seriously hurting your job search, it's okay to go all in.

practice: I'm job-hunting while still employed, which gives me more leverage.
表达「把面试安排在非工作时间」
I'll schedule interviews in the evenings or on weekends.
Negotiating is easier when they're trying to win you over.
If work is blocking my search, I'll go all in and quit.
pitfalls: ✕ 直译腔：Quit first and then look for a job.
✓ 地道说法：Don't resign blindly—hunt while you're still employed.
裸辞是 resign blindly / quit without a plan。
✕ 直译腔：I have enough bottom energy.
✓ 地道说法：Being employed gives me more leverage.
底气是 leverage，不是 bottom energy。
✕ 直译腔：No security and no sense of safety.
✓ 地道说法：No safety net, and that's scary.
安全感用 safety net，更具体。
✓ 地道说法：It's okay to go all in and focus on the search.
放手一搏用 go all in。
shifts: 在职求职+时间管理双轨推进
把在职谈判优势算进决策
用求职进度与时间占用判断
footer_notes: ASR 校正：原文「人设的极限」按语境校正为「忍耐的极限」，「改警令」校正为「改简历」，「轻重环节」校正为「轻重缓急」，「斥舍」校正为「取舍」，「完成几站」校正为「严重挤占」。场景/句子朗读使用 edge-tts，单词发音使用浏览器 Web Speech API。
